summary: Duplicate external webhook executions caused by trace-id / idempotency normalization across proxies and mixed SDKs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated executions of their webhook endpoint (external tool) when Redwood function-calling invokes it. Impact: duplicate downstream side-effects (duplicate invoices/notifications). Initial suspicion: SDK retry duplicates.

Impact: Several customer customers reported duplicate charges and notifications over a ~12-hour window. Quantile Insights (enterprise) has paused production traffic.

Environment: production, us-east, using a mix of client integrations — an internal orchestration service (Go SDK) and a server-side Python worker (Python SDK). Requests originate from our hosted API through the customer's public webhook (behind their ALB).

Observed behavior: Redwood logs show the function-call acknowledged once, but the customer endpoint received 2-3 identical POSTs within seconds. Timestamps indicate the second delivery came after a 502/timeout from the ALB to the customer, followed by a retry from our side. The idempotency header observed at the customer differed between the first and retry deliveries (different representation of same trace token).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer registers webhook URL behind an ALB that performs header normalization (ALB rewrites certain characters).
2) Client triggers a function-call via Redwood API (Go SDK) with an idempotency token populated by SDK (x-redwood-idempotency).

3) During the first delivery ALB accepts request and forwards; if ALB returns a 502 due to transient backend issue, Redwood retries delivery using the same idempotency value but the ALB normalizes '+' characters to space or strips certain chars, changing the header representation seen by the customer endpoint.
4) Customer endpoint's idempotency dedupe logic uses raw header string; because header representation changed, dedupe fails and webhook processes both requests.
logs: 2026-03-13T18:02:11Z - function-call id=fc_01AB: outbound POST to https://hooks.quantile/notify - attempt=1 - x-redwood-idempotency=Zm9vK3JhbmQ=
2026-03-13T18:02:12Z - gateway error from ALB upstream: 502 Bad Gateway - marking attempt failed
2026-03-13T18:02:12Z - retrying delivery attempt=2 - x-redwood-idempotency=Zm9v/kw= (observed on our side)
2026-03-13T18:02:12Z - delivery acked by customer endpoint - status=200
Customer logs provided: 2026-03-13T18:02:12Z - Received webhook POST - header 'X-Idemp': 'Zm9v rand' (note: '+' replaced with space) -> processed
Customer logs provided: 2026-03-13T18:02:12Z - Received webhook POST - header 'X-Idemp': 'Zm9v/kw=' -> processed (duplicate)
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Not a plain SDK double-send. Redwood shows single canonical function execution. Duplicates occur during outbound webhook delivery retries.
Hypothesis: Intermediate proxy (ALB or on-prem proxy) is normalizing base64/idempotency header values (e.g., '+' characters converted or stripped), causing customer-side dedupe to miss matches.
Cross-checked headers captured by our gateway vs customer-provided logs: representations differ consistently when a proxy sits between our gateway and the customer app.

Reproduced in staging by placing an ALB with default settings in front of a test webhook service: when ALB rewrites headers the exact token value changes but decode(original) == decode(transformed) only if proxy performs URL-decoding; in many cases customer-side dedupe treats strings raw.

SDKs differ in idempotency token generation: Go SDK uses base64 URL encoding without padding in some versions while Python SDK uses standard base64 with padding. Combined with proxy normalization, representations diverge.
Security check: No evidence of malicious replay. Timestamps and signatures match original payloads; duplicates caused by header transformation semantics.
resolution:
Short-term workaround provided to customer: (1) Implement idempotency dedupe using a canonicalized form (e.g., normalize URL-safe base64 -> standard base64 or compute SHA256 of payload+token) so proxy differences are tolerated; (2) Configure ALB to preserve header characters (disable header normalization) or route via a pass-through proxy.

Planned fixes: (a) Add server-side canonicalization and de-dup window for function-call webhook deliveries so equivalent tokens with different permitted encodings are treated as identical for 60s by default. (b) Create SDK guidance: standardize on URL-safe base64 without padding across Go/Python/TS SDKs and add opt-in helper to compute canonical idempotency token. (c) Backport small change to api-gateway to emit an additional canonical header x-redwood-idempotency-canonical (sha256) for customers to use when implementing dedupe behind proxies.

Rollout notes: config flag in gateway to enable canonical header; patch scheduled for canary 2026-03-17, full rollout 2026-03-24 after customer validation.

Customer follow-up: Quantile agreed to deploy the canonical dedupe change and re-enable traffic after canary patch.
comments: 2026-03-13 - Support (Ayesha): Received duplicate delivery reports from Quantile; opening ticket with Eng and Networking. Asked for full webhook headers and example payloads.
2026-03-13 - Customer (Quantile Ops): Provided webhook logs and stack trace. Noted duplicates only when ALB in front of webhook. Already using per-request idempotency header for dedupe.
2026-03-13 - SRE (Marco): Reproduced header rewrite in staging ALB; ALB docs show header character normalization for certain encodings.
2026-03-14 - SDK Team (Lina): Investigating unifying idempotency token format across SDKs; proposed URL-safe base64 w/o padding as canonical standard.
2026-03-14 - Support (Ayesha): Shared workaround steps with customer and validated their dedupe shim accepted canonical sha256 header. Customer confirmed no duplicates during 2-hour test window.
2026-03-14 - Engineering (Marco): Filed PRs to add x-redwood-idempotency-canonical header and guidance in SDK docs. Will monitor canary metrics for duplicate deliveries.
2026-03-14 - Customer (Quantile Ops): Requested ETA for full rollout; asked for communication plan in advance of change.
